LAB NOTES / A TWO-MINUTE TOUR

Chat. Catch a glitch. Check the evidence.

01

Send a message

Tell the AI a project name, budget, or plan. Ask a follow-up. Your original words stay in the paper trail, and each reply is checked against them. With Chaos on, the first two replies stay normal. Every third reply adds absurd commentary and a reaction meme, then the cycle repeats. These scheduled reactions are entertainment. Evidence-backed memory alerts appear immediately, on any reply. Use the CHAOS switch for plain replies.

02

Try a checked glitch

Open Scripted demo for a guaranteed sample mistake: a fixed AI reply contradicts an earlier registration message. The checker runs live. If the issue is confirmed, a meme arrives with the exact quotes and a correction. This is a demonstration, not a spontaneous AI failure.

03

Run the real forgetting test

The Memory Test Lab ↗ makes three real model calls with 20, 10, then 0 facts. Expand the answers and input receipts to see exactly what was provided. Unknown answers and wrong answers are counted separately.

Open real test lab ↗
What the checker actually does

The conversation model and the independent checker receive separate contexts. After a reply, the checker looks for a clear contradiction or a failure to recall something your records answer. Both quoted passages must exist in the original text, and a second check must confirm the issue. A confirmed issue gets a memory-alert meme and a useful correction. Scheduled chat reactions appear every third Chaos-enabled reply, are labelled separately, and do not imply an error. Meme captions are kept out of future conversation context.

Checks can miss issues or flag them incorrectly. A changed plan is not a contradiction. Your words are evidence of what you said, not external verification. This page cannot inspect ChatGPT or Codex's internal context or predict when a model is about to forget.

See controlled context removal in the Memory Test Lab ↗
